title: Maximum Number of Fish in a Grid
summary: Given a 0-indexed 2D matrix grid of size m x n, where each cell (r, c) is either a land cell with grid[r][c] = 0 or a water cell containing grid[r][c] fish, a fisher can start at any water cell and perform the following actions any number of times: - Catch all the fish at the current water cell, or - Move to any adjacent water cell.
statement: Given a 0-indexed 2D matrix grid of size m x n, where each cell (r, c) is either a land cell with grid[r][c] = 0 or a water cell containing grid[r][c] fish, a fisher can start at any water cell and perform the following actions any number of times: - Catch all the fish at the current water cell, or - Move to any adjacent water cell. Determine the maximum number of fish the fisher can catch by optimally choosing the starting water cell, or return 0 if no water cells are present. An adjacent cell to (r, c) includes (r, c + 1), (r, c - 1), (r + 1, c), or (r - 1, c) if they exist.
constraints: Zero cells are land; positive cells are water containing that many fish.
A fisher may start at any water cell and move four-directionally through water cells, collecting all fish visited.
Return the greatest fish total in one connected water component, or zero if none exists.
hints: Each starting point can reach exactly one four-connected positive component.
Scan all cells and flood-fill every unseen water cell once.
Sum cell values during each fill and retain the largest component sum.
Components partition all water cells, so considering each component once covers every possible start and its maximum collectable total.
editorial: Components partition all water cells, so considering each component once covers every possible start and its maximum collectable total.

tests.explanation: The right-side water component contains three and four fish for total seven.
The lower component totals six fish, exceeding the isolated one.
